ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1.

Present petition is directed against the order passed by the Collector dated 13.03.2023 in rejecting the representation moved by the petitioner seeking for release of the acquired land in terms of section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

It is argued by learned counsel for the petitioner that Makodbhai Bhanabhai Jadapiya vs State Of Gujarat on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111997079/

sentences.text: in the first round of litigation initiated by the petitioner, vide judgement and order dated 07.03.2023, this Court has relegated the petitioner to approach the petitioner to approach the competent authority by moving a representation agitating the demand for release of the land.

The NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/19355/2023 ORDER DATED: 07/11/2023 undefined submission is that section 48 confers the power on the State Government to withdraw from acquisition and the Collector, having no power to take a decision in the matter of withdrawal from acquisition of the land in question in terms of Section 48, was not empowered to make an inquiry or reject the representation.
2. Dealing with this contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner, relevant is to note that there is no dispute about the fact that acquisition of the land in question is complete with the proceedings drawn in the year 2001-2002, itself.
The petitioner herein had received compensation under the award for the acquired land.

In the year 2021, Special Civil Application 15090 of 2021 had been filed by the petitioner seeking for release of his land from an acquisition on the premise that the land in question had not been utilized by Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation for its purpose.
The prayer was that the land being unutilized was required to be released in his favour.
In the said writ petition vide judgement and order dated 7.03.2023 direction was issued to the petitioner to approach the competent authority.

In the result, the application was filed before the Collector seeking for release of the land wherein the communication dated 13.03.2023 was issued to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/19355/2023 ORDER DATED: 07/11/2023 undefined the petitioner.
The perusal of the communication issued by the Collector indicates that the land in question is being used as Gauchar land at the present.

The land, in question, which was initially acquired for the purposes of Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation, had been exchanged with the Gram Panchayat under Section 38 of the Land Revenue Code,1894, vide order dated 15.11.2016.

The land,
in question, thus, is still being used for the public purposes.

The communication further records that under the award dated 05.01.2004 the petitioner had received compensation.
3. It is settled law that once the acquired land is vested with the State Government, it can be utilized for any other public purposes than the purposes for which it was acquired.

It is well settled that after the possession of the land is taken and the land acquisition proceedings are brought to its logical,
even the State Government is denuded of its powers to release the acquired land by invoking the provisions of Section 48, which only talks of withdrawal of an acquisition before the completion of the acquisition proceedings.

Reference in this regard be made to this Court in the case of Sanmukhbhai Bhikhabhai Patel and others vs. State of Gujarat and others reported in 2005 (1)
G.L.H.707.

sentences.text: A careful reading of section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, clearly indicates that it gives power to the State Government to withdraw from the acquisition at any stage of the proceedings before possession of the acquired land is taken.
The question to determine compensation for the damages suffered by the owner, as per sub-section (2) of Section 48 would arise only in a case where Government withdraws from any such acquisition.

In the said scenario, the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the decision on the representation filed by the petitioner is beyond the jurisdiction of the Collector, inasmuch as, the power to withdraw from acquisition lies with the State Government under Section 48 of the Act, 1894, does not appeal to us.

In this case, on the representation moved by the petitioner, the factual information has been transmitted to the petitioner with regard to the status of the land in question by the communication dated 1303.2023.
5. The prayer made by the petitioner seeking for quashing of the communication made by the petitioner and release of the acquired land, therefore, cannot be entertained.
6. The writ petition is accordingly dismissed, being devoid of merits.
